detail.title: Synthesis: Humor as Predictive Incongruity Resolution
detail.summary: Humor arises when the brain encounters a prediction error that is benignly resolved, re-calibrating the internal model of expected stimuli.
detail.reason: This notebook synthesizes the distinct mechanisms of incongruity and prediction error identified in the source literature.

detail.title: Synthesis: Predictive Self-Continuity
detail.summary: Self-continuity is maintained not by the preservation of static states, but by the continuous, iterative calibration of an internal model of the self against temporal sensory data.
detail.reason: This notebook establishes a preliminary model of identity as an active, predictive construct rather than a static record.
